messages:
Maya: FYI running into a nasty behavior with the sampleapp's paginator + Go SDK. During onboarding demo it blew up our staging quota and created a sudden surge of concurrent requests.
Liam: Ugh. Can you paste the pattern? is it client-side parallel pagination?
Maya: It's the default sampleapp use: we iterate pages and spawn a goroutine per page to process items. Works fine normally but when a 401 (token refresh) or 429 hits, the retry logic immediately retries without coordination and all goroutines flood the API.
Maya: Repro steps: run sample-app against a dataset that pages ~200 pages, throttle the token endpoint (simulate slow KMS), then introduce a transient 429 on a middle page.
Ryan: That sounds like two problems stacked: token refresh race + paginator spawning unbounded concurrency.
Sara: Did the Go SDK not singleflight token refresh? I thought we had a mutex there.
Maya: The SDK has a singleflight-ish refresh, but sampleapp uses its own auth wrapper and calls client.NewRequest(...) per goroutine so the short window where the cached token is expired results in ~N refresh attempts.
Liam: Oof. So sampleapp bypasses the SDK helper and reimplements auth, which is the root cause.
Maya: Yep. Also the paginator in sampleapp has concurrency=0 which we treat as "max parallel" by using a fan-out pattern which makes things worse.
Ryan: Quick mitigation: respect Retry-After from 429, add exponential backoff with jitter, and cap paginator concurrency (eg 4).
Sara: +1. Also add a singleflight/sync.Once style token refresh in the sampleapp auth wrapper, or better, use the SDK's auth client directly.
Maya: I sketched a minimal fix. Code snippet: ```go // simple singleflight token refresh var refreshMu sync.Mutex func getToken(ctx context.Context) (string, error) { refreshMu.Lock() defer refreshMu.Unlock() if tokenValid(cached) { return cached, nil } t, err := realRefresh(ctx) if err != nil { return "", err } cached = t return t, nil } ```
Liam: That will serialise refreshes but still could block many goroutines — combine it with a leaky bucket limiter for outgoing requests.
Ryan: For paginator change: make the iterator yield pages synchronously by default, and provide an optional WithParallelPages(n) config. For sampleapp we should default to 2-4.
Maya: Also important: SDK should expose a recommended backoff policy and helper middleware so sample apps don't reimplement fragile logic.
Sara: Agreed. We should update docs and the quickstart template too. It currently shows naive parallel processing.
Maya: I captured logs — DeployBot posted the quota alert at the time: "DeployBot: quota-billing: project-dev exceeded user rate by 120% (alerts suppressed 2m)"
Liam: Can you add a test that simulates slow token endpoint and 429 spikes? we can add it to the devex sampleapp CI.
Maya: Will do. Plan: 1) patch sampleapp to use SDK auth client 2) cap paginator concurrency to 3 3) add jittered exponential backoff honoring Retry-After 4) add an integration test that throttles endpoints. I'll open a PR after tests.
Ryan: If you want I can review the concurrency patch — also let's add a telemetry tag so we can see "paginator.concurrency" in Console.
Maya: Good idea. I'll emit a small metric when the paginator is created.
Sara: FYI note for product: this is likely a common onboarding pain. maybe change quickstart wording to call out concurrency/backoff best practices.
Maya: Thanks all — making the patch now. I'll ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
Liam: Thanks Maya. small follow-up: add a short blurb in the SDK README about using sdk.BackoffPolicy and not reinventing auth.
Maya: Adding that too.
DeployBot: [automated] Created incident link: https://redwood.example/incident/INC-2028 - rate-limit storm from onboarding sample app
Ryan: Nice. Once PR is up I'll run the throttling test locally and sanity-check metrics.
Maya: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/512 (WIP) — includes concurrency cap + singleflight auth example.
Sara: Great. After merge we should swap the quickstart to reference the new sample app tag.
Maya: Will follow up.
